title: The landed rollback is hardened: previous image redeployed without rebuild, atomic order proven by mutation, recovery proven through the real probe
description:
SPIDR successor of task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4, cut by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05. That row carried backups, a new human-only command kind and this effect; the kind alone is a two-row roster job on this board, so the three were separated. This row is the EFFECT: it owns the parent's DoD 5, 6 and 7.

dependsOn: task-b22462cf (the wired kind, whose fail-closed stub this row replaces), task-95e68a8d (the backups this row optionally restores from), and task-6ec875f4 (the probe that confirms recovery).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `deployment.rollback {environment, toReceiptRef}` actually rolling back - resolving the previous image from the KEPT DEPLOY RECEIPT, redeploying it with the same atomic replace and health probe the forward deploy uses, restoring the database backup ONLY when explicitly requested, and confirming recovery through the real probe.

NEVER REBUILD AN IMAGE TO SATISFY A ROLLBACK. This is the row's hardest rule and the one most likely to be softened under pressure: a rebuild from source under the same sha produces a DIFFERENT image, so an environment "rolled back" that way is running bytes nobody has ever run. When the receipt names an image that no longer exists locally, the honest answer is `ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING` - a refusal, not a rebuild.

THE RECEIPT SHAPE IS A SIBLING'S, NOT THIS ROW'S. task-c0e00f0a (the deploy engine) stores the kept deploy receipt and its completion record is required to NAME the retrieval call for exactly this reason - that row is a sibling and cannot be depended on, so read its completionSummary and build against what actually shipped rather than what was designed.

REUSE THE FORWARD DEPLOY'S ATOMIC REPLACE. A rollback that replaces differently from a deploy is a second lifecycle to reason about during an incident, which is precisely when nobody has the patience for two. The switch point, the health probe and the teardown all come from the deploy engine.

NOT IN SCOPE: the backups themselves (task-95e68a8d), the command kind's roster and fence (task-37a50989 and task-b22462cf), the probe (task-6ec875f4), and the incident card UI (task-f008f29a).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: HARDEN THE LANDED ROLLBACK (governor amendment 21:25Z, worker-deb4c7d8's measurement: `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts` (171 lines, registered at daemon-command-async-entries.ts:281) and `deploy-service.ts:300-308` ALREADY implement the effect; this row lands NO second implementation and creates no `repository/deployment/deployment-rollback*` file - global rail 6). DoD 1: the rollback resolves the PREVIOUS IMAGE TAG from the kept deploy receipt and redeploys THAT image - asserted offline through the injectable docker port's recorded argv, byte-for-byte, and the tag EQUALS the value READ BACK from the previous receipt, never a fixture constant that agrees with itself.

IT NEVER REBUILDS: enumerate EVERY recorded argv and assert the absence of any build verb on every rollback path (not merely `builds === []` on one path). When the receipt names an image absent locally, the tree's code `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` is asserted with code AND layer.

DATABASE RESTORE: the production restore destination does not exist today (rollback-command.ts:86-88 refuses `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`; `BackupPorts.restoreDatabase` only verifies into a temporary isolated database) - moved to the split row filed 21:25Z. THIS row asserts: `restore: true` refuses with that code AND layer; `restore` not requested records NO restore call on the port (read the recorded calls, never trust a flag).

THE ATOMIC REPLACE IS THE FORWARD DEPLOY'S (rollback calls `execute(...)` with the rollback image - one lifecycle): assert through the port's recorded call ORDER that the old container serves until the new one answers health, with no point at which neither serves. MUTATION DRILL REQUIRED: swap to a stop-then-start order and quote the arm's failing line - an ordering property never seen red is not evidence.

AFTER A ROLLBACK THE REAL PROBE CONFIRMS RECOVERY: the environment returns to UP through the landed probe path (task-e651725c / task-cc05c473's ring and scheduler), asserted through that path - not an internal flag and not the docker double's own state.

REFUSALS ARE THE TREE'S: `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_INVALID` and `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` each assert code AND layer (the already-rostered layer stamped by DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP, deploy-service.ts:78); introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant and rename no dispatched code. The 'fail-closed stub' this DoD once named does not exist - say so in the completion record with the grep.

EVERY container, temp directory and child process the tests create is released on EVERY exit path INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE - teardown in a `finally`, never after the assertions. No test reaches the network or a real docker daemon. Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NEVER REBUILD AN IMAGE TO SATISFY A ROLLBACK. A rebuild under the same sha is a different image, and an environment running bytes nobody has ever run is worse than a refusal. A missing image is ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING.
THE DATABASE IS RESTORED ONLY WHEN EXPLICITLY REQUESTED. A silent restore is data loss the operator did not ask for, and the not-requested path is asserted as untouched.
REUSE THE FORWARD DEPLOY'S ATOMIC REPLACE, health probe and teardown. A second lifecycle is a second thing to reason about during an incident.
THE DEPLOY RECEIPT'S SHAPE IS A SIBLING'S (task-c0e00f0a) AND CANNOT BE DEPENDED ON. Read its completionSummary and build against what shipped, not against what was designed.
OFFLINE TESTS ONLY, every port injectable, and everything started is stopped on every exit path including the throwing one.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE LANDED SURFACE BEFORE WRITING AN ARM. This row adds NO production code (governor amendment 21:25Z, DoD 1); every clause is an assertion or a drill over what already ships. Record each command and its output — DoD 6 requires the completion record to state, with the grep, that the 'fail-closed stub' does not exist.

Run and quote:
- `git grep -rln "deployment-rollback" -- apps packages` — expect NO output. That is the stub grep. Create no `repository/deployment/deployment-rollback*` file.
- `wc -l apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts` — expect 171.
- `sed -n '346,357p' apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` — confirm `rollback` ends in `execute({...}, selected.receipt.imageDigest)`, i.e. the forward deploy's own lifecycle.
- `sed -n '283,297p' apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` — confirm the build/transfer block is inside `if (rollbackImage === undefined)` and that `:296` passes `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` as the DETAIL under code `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`.
- `git status --porcelain` the three paths this row owns; note peer dirt and leave it alone.

If `rollback` no longer routes through `execute`, or a `deployment-rollback*` file now exists, STOP and report — the row's premise has moved.

DoD 2 — IT NEVER REBUILDS, ON EVERY PATH. The existing `expect(context.builds).toEqual([])` covers ONE path; DoD 2 says that is not enough.

Add a sweep helper in `deploy-rollback.test.ts` that enumerates EVERY recorded argv (`context.docker.calls`, the ordered `readonly (readonly string[])[]` at deploy-ports.ts:266) and asserts no entry's verb is a build verb: `build`, `buildx`, `save`, `load`, `pull`, `commit`, `import`. Assert the `build` and `transfer`/`ssh` ports recorded nothing either — `harness()` already captures `builds`.

RUN THE SWEEP ON EVERY ROLLBACK PATH, each as its own arm: success, image-missing (`harness(true)`), unhealthy candidate (`harness(false, false)`), wrong environment, and the replay path. A sweep is only evidence if it is applied where a rebuild could plausibly hide.

GUARD AGAINST A VACUOUS SWEEP (global rail: a generated case that yields zero cases passes): assert `context.docker.calls.length` is greater than zero before sweeping it, on every path where a call is expected. On the wrong-environment path the tree refuses before any Docker effect, so assert `calls` is EMPTY there explicitly rather than letting the sweep pass on nothing.

DRILL: make the engine take the build branch on a rollback (delete the `rollbackImage === undefined` guard around the build block) and confirm the sweep reds on the success path; restore and prove with `git diff`.

DoD 3 — THE DATABASE RESTORE, ASSERTED FROM RECORDED CALLS. The production restore destination does not exist (moved to the row split off 21:25Z); `rollback-command.ts:86-89` refuses `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`. This row asserts two things in `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.test.ts`.

(a) `restoreDatabase: true` refuses with that code AND the layer it is thrown at — `DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` (`refuse()` at :24-26 stamps it). The existing table row at :50 pins the code by name only; add the layer. Also assert the refusal happens BEFORE any effect: `rollback-command.ts:88` refuses ahead of `readDeployReceipt`, so assert the docker double recorded ZERO calls and no deploy receipt was written on that path.

(b) `restoreDatabase: false` records NO restore call on the backup port — READ THE RECORDED CALLS, never trust the flag (DoD 3 says so explicitly). Inject a backup-port double that appends to an array and assert that array is empty after a successful rollback, while asserting the rollback itself succeeded so the arm is not passing on a path that never ran.

DRILL (b): make the handler call `restoreDatabase` unconditionally and confirm the arm reds — an "asserted untouched" arm that has never seen a call is indistinguishable from one whose port is never wired. Restore and prove with `git diff`.

DoD 5 — RECOVERY THROUGH THE REAL PROBE, in a new file `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-recovery-probe.test.ts`. Kept separate from the engine test so the temp-directory lifecycle stays local and obvious (DoD 7).

Drive the landed monitoring path, not an internal flag and not the docker double's own state:
- `createHealthProbeRing(path, projectId)` (`monitoring/health-probe-ring.ts:93`) over a real temp directory;
- `probeEnvironment({...})` (:191) with an injected `HealthHttpPort` (`(url, signal) => Promise<number>`, :131) — the port resolves through the docker double's `upstream()` so a 200 means the environment really is serving the rolled-back container, rather than a hardcoded success;
- `deriveHealthState(ring.read())` (:125-126) is the assertion surface: it returns `"UP"` only when the latest probe is `SUCCESS`.

ARC: environment healthy -> incumbent becomes unhealthy so a probe records a non-SUCCESS and `deriveHealthState` is NOT `"UP"` -> perform the rollback through the engine -> probe again -> assert `deriveHealthState` is now `"UP"`. Asserting the DOWN state first is what makes the recovery assertion mean something; an arm that only ever sees `"UP"` would pass against a probe that always succeeds.

TEARDOWN IN A `finally`, NEVER AFTER THE ASSERTIONS (DoD 7 and epic rail 4): remove the temp directory with `{ recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 20, retryDelay: 100 }` and close the ring on the throwing path too. No network, no real docker daemon, every port injected.

NOTE the flagged collision is spurious and stay clear of it: claim_next_task warned on `repository/deployment/deployment-docker-probe.ts` (shared with task-99f364e3), but that module is docker-DAEMON availability (`probeDocker`, `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`), a different subject from this health probe. Neither read nor edit it.

GATES (DoD 7), ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (Skill `adversarial-self-review`), AND PATH DECLARATION.

Acquire `full-suite-gate` for the full legs (one full suite at a time on this host); announce GATE START/END with the UTC window and release on EVERY exit path including failure. Every drill in steps 2-6 happens OUTSIDE the lease — they mutate shared files on disk. Run each leg standalone and foreground; never pipe and never `;`-chain, because a pipe reports tail's status and a chain only the last command's:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — the row's named verification command. Quote `Test Files N passed (N)`; exit 0 alone is not evidence and a filter that matches nothing also exits 0.
2. `pnpm typecheck` — EXIT 0 with a planted-error control in a NEW file to prove the leg is not short-circuiting; delete the planted file and show the clean re-run.
The root lane covers no `apps/**` file, so do not quote a bare root `pnpm test` count line as evidence for anything here.

TEARDOWN AUDIT before you call it done: grep your new and edited arms for every `mkdtemp`, container start and child process, and confirm each is released in a `finally` rather than after the assertions. Re-run the daemon leg twice in a row — a leaked temp directory or container usually surfaces as an EPERM or a name collision on the second run, not the first.

Adversarial pass, aimed at this row's specific holes: does the DoD 1 arm still pass if the engine ignores the receipt (it must not — you drilled it)? Does the build sweep run on a path where `calls` is empty and pass vacuously? Does the DoD 4 ordering arm actually go red under the stop-then-start mutation (quote the line)? Does the DoD 3 not-requested arm distinguish "port never called" from "port never wired"? Is any drilled mutation still on disk — `git diff` all three production files you touched during drills and confirm each is empty?

Record in the completion summary, with the grep, that no fail-closed stub exists and that no production code was added. Declare EXACTLY the files changed via complete_step.modifiedFiles / moe.declare_files.

COORDINATION from task-b7cdf265's planning (architect-d6d49adc, 2026-09-07). Read before planning this row — one of your assertions changes meaning, and one shared file is touched.

WHAT CHANGES. task-b7cdf265 (now planned, auto-approved) removes the UNCONDITIONAL refusal at `rollback-command.ts:86-89`. Today `if (request.restore) refuse(DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE, ...)` fires for EVERY restore, before the deploy receipt is even read. After that row it fires only when the environment has NO BOUND RESTORE DESTINATION.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR DoD. Your row's description says you keep "the refusal's code+layer assertion and the no-restore-call assertion". Both survive, but the first one narrows: it must be asserted for an UNBOUND environment, not for any `restoreDatabase: true`. An arm that asserts "restore always refuses" will go RED once b7cdf265 lands, and it would be wrong to fix that by reverting the binding. b7cdf265's step 6 (c) keeps exactly that unbound-environment arm green, so the coverage does not disappear — it moves to the case that is still true.

The no-restore-call assertion is unaffected and gets stronger: b7cdf265 step 6 (b) asserts ZERO recorded calls on the restore port when `restoreDatabase: false`, from the port's recorded calls rather than from the absence of a failure.

SHARED FILES. b7cdf265 owns `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts`, `rollback-command.test.ts` and `rollback-production-wiring.test.ts`. It changes ONLY the database arm of the command — replay identity, the intent record, the environment guard leg and receipt validation are left exactly as they are, and the IMAGE-side rollback hardening (previous image redeployed without rebuild) is explicitly left to this row. If your plan needs those same files, re-read them at your HEAD before editing rather than planning against today's lines, and consider declaring dependsOn on b7cdf265 so the two do not land into each other in the shared worktree.

ONE MEASURED FACT THAT MAY SAVE YOU A DERIVATION: the deploy receipt has NO `backupRef` — RECEIPT_KEYS (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:82-85) is twelve keys and none of them is a backup. `backupRef` lives only on the MIGRATION receipt, reached by the durable join DEPLOY RECEIPT `decisionId` === MIGRATION RECEIPT `requestId` (`deploy-command.ts:267`), resolvable via `migrationReceiptId` / `readMigrationReceipt`. If any part of your hardening needs to name the backup a deploy took, that is the join — not a filename or timestamp match.

THE EFFECT IS LANDED AND THE GOVERNOR AMENDMENT IS CORRECT. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts` is 171 lines and `deploy-service.ts:346-357` implements `rollback`. THIS ROW ADDS NO PRODUCTION CODE — every DoD clause is an assertion or a drill over what already ships. WHY DoD 2 AND DoD 4 ARE ALREADY STRUCTURALLY TRUE (assert them; do not re-implement them):
`deploy-service.ts:356` — `rollback` ends in `return execute({ context: "", decisionId, environment, sha: selected.receipt.sha }, selected.receipt.imageDigest)`. It calls THE FORWARD DEPLOY'S OWN `execute`, passing the kept receipt's `imageDigest` as the `rollbackImage` argument. Inside `execute`, `:283` `const tag = rollbackImage ?? deployImageTag(environment, sha)` and `:284-292` wraps the ENTIRE build-and-transfer block in `if (rollbackImage === undefined)`. THE REFUSAL TRIPLE, AND DoD 2's PHRASING IS INACCURATE — THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING HERE. DoD 2 calls `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE` "the tree's code". The plan asserts the FULL TRIPLE and records the discrepancy — that satisfies DoD 2's intent ("the tree's" refusal, pinned by code AND layer) without renaming anything.
By contrast `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_INVALID` IS a real code (`deploy-service.ts:38`, returned at `:351` and thrown at the seam by `rollback-command.ts`), rostered at `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:125` @ `DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` and asserted at `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:442`.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE SELF-AGREEING FIXTURE IS THE TRAP DoD 1 NAMES, and the existing test already falls into it. `digest` is a module constant used BOTH to seed the receipt and to assert the argv, so the arm passes even if the engine ignored the receipt entirely. Read the tag back with `readDeployReceipt(store, projectId, request.receiptId)` inside the assertion and compare the argv to THAT. Drill it: seed the receipt with a second, different digest and confirm the arm reds.
2. AN ORDERING ARM NEVER SEEN RED IS NOT EVIDENCE (DoD 4 says so explicitly). The drill is mandatory: swap `execute`'s order so the incumbent stops before the candidate is healthy, quote the failing line verbatim, restore, and prove restoration with `git diff` (tracked path). Do not hold `full-suite-gate` while an on-disk mutation is live — announce the UTC window instead.
3. A BUILD-VERB SWEEP THAT GENERATES ZERO CASES PASSES. Assert the sweep actually ran: check the enumerated argv count is non-zero before asserting no entry starts with a build verb. Cover `build`, `buildx`, `save`, `load`, `pull`, `commit`, `import`, and the transfer/ssh port — and run it on EVERY rollback path (success, image-missing, unhealthy-candidate, wrong-environment, replay), not just the happy one.
4. DoD 3's not-requested path must be read from RECORDED CALLS on the backup port, never from the boolean. `rollback-command.ts:88` refuses BEFORE the receipt is even read, so on the `restore: true` path nothing else runs — assert that too, or the arm proves less than it looks.
5. TEARDOWN IN `finally`, NOT AFTER THE ASSERTIONS (DoD 7). The DoD 5 arm creates a real temp directory for the probe ring; a throwing assertion must still remove it, and the ring's file handle must be closed on the throwing path. An arm that leaks a temp dir makes every later gate on this board inadmissible (epic rail 4).
6. `deploy-rollback.test.ts` is 75 lines and `rollback-command.test.ts` is 226. Neither is near the 400 cap, but keep the new arms tight rather than duplicating the harness — extend the existing `harness()` with parameters instead of copying it.
7. Shared checkout: `git status --porcelain` the three paths before editing; never revert, stash or commit a foreign path.
